overall: Atlanta had a hotter-than-model-expected day, with the running maximum reaching 91.4°F around 16:19 ET before a sharp convective boundary dropped temperatures dramatically — from ~89-90°F at 16:52 down to 80.6°F by 17:52, almost certainly triggered by the severe thunderstorm activity that prompted active NWS warnings across the area. By 21:00 ET, temperatures are at 80.6°F with a cooling velocity of -1.8°F/hr, confirming the day's peak is well behind us. The Severe Thunderstorm Watch and expired Severe Thunderstorm Warning for north/central Georgia are consistent with this abrupt afternoon temperature crash.
forecast_obs_notes: All NWP models significantly underforecast today's actual high — ECMWF (87.5°F) and NBM (86.8°F) missed by roughly 4°F, while HRRR (90.1°F) was the closest but still ~1.3°F short of the observed 91.4°F running max. This widespread underprediction suggests unusually strong daytime mixing or boundary-layer heating ahead of the convective initiation, a classic pattern on unstable high-dewpoint days where the cap breaks late.
max_temp_prediction: The daily TMAX is effectively locked at 91.4°F with very high confidence — this is the confirmed running maximum, it occurred roughly 4.7 hours ago, and with current temps at 80.6°F and falling through the evening with active convection, there is essentially zero probability of a new daytime high occurring tonight. The INTRADAY model's 96.8% concentration in the 90-91°F bucket aligns tightly with the observed running max, and the give-up classifier fired at 14.67h when the running max was already 89.6°F, correctly anticipating that the peak was near. Best estimate is 91.4°F.
